messages:
Mira K: heads-up — customer reported rerank results look scrambled when we send >1 query in the same batch. scores are present but seem shifted between queries.
Alex R: ugh, can you paste the request they used?
Mira K: sending sanitized payload below — they batch 3 queries with different candidate counts, we return a flat scores array that doesn't line up with per-query candidates.
Mira K: ```json
{
  "queries": ["q1 text", "q2 text", "q3 text"],
  "candidates": ["c1", "c2", "c3", "c4", "c5", "c6"],
  "per_query_counts": [2, 1, 3],
  "options": {"method": "batch-rerank"}
}
```
Mira K: client expects 2 scores for q1, 1 for q2, 3 for q3. what we returned looked like 1,3,2 instead (shifted).
Jessica L: do we have the response body? any headers?
Mira K: response 200 with scores array length 6. server log shows no error. curl they used: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" --data-binary @payload.json --compressed`
SRE Jon: noting `--compressed` — could be gzip interplay but if body is decompressed by gateway we still parse. any chance the client flattened candidates incorrectly before sending?
Alex R: i reproduced locally by sending the same payload and saw score offsets when I hit our dedicated gateway (route: /v1/rerank/batch -> runtime:batch). when I force send without compression it works. with gzip it fails.
Alex R: possible hypothesis: our request body parser for the batch endpoint mishandles multi-part buffer boundaries after decompression, concatenating candidate offsets incorrectly into a single flat index.
Jessica L: can you dump the raw decompressed JSON we receive vs what the client sent?
Alex R: yep — here are diffs:
client raw file: `...[per_query_counts: 2,1,3]`
server parsed: `...[per_query_counts: 1,3,2]`
Mira K: the customer sent via a Python requests session with `headers={"Accept-Encoding": "gzip"}` and `json=payload`.
SRE Jon: does the compressor reorder arrays? unlikely. more likely a bug in our streaming JSON parser when fed chunked gzip streams — arrays might be merged incorrectly if chunk boundary splits numbers/comma tokens.
eng-runtime: tagging runtime team — this looks like a streaming parse edge-case. can you attach a minimal repro?
Alex R: created a tiny repro script that gzips the payload then pipes it with different chunk sizes. failing pattern reproduced when chunk size < 512 bytes. added repro gist: https://internal/gists/rr-repro-2054
eng-runtime: thanks. can you include the exact curl and the raw bytes we received (hex)? we'll triage.
Mira K: customer is high priority — affecting production batch scoring for two customers. they also reported a spike in latency on these batch calls when compressed.
Jessica L: billing/limits question: did this increase token usage or cause duplicate charges?
Mira K: no duplicate billing reported; token usage recorded normally. but because scores mismatch, they retried several times which increased usage manually.
SRE Jon: mitigation: ask clients to avoid `Accept-Encoding: gzip` for now or send uncompressed payloads. also set server-side feature-flag to disable streaming parser for batch-rerank until patch.
Alex R: opened INC-4862 and engineering PR: https://repo/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/879 — patch switches to non-streaming parse for arrays in the rerank endpoint and adds chunk-boundary tests.
eng-runtime: we'll roll a canary to staging in ~30m. need support to notify this customer of a temporary workaround and ETA.
Mira K: I'll message them with workaround and offer to replay their payloads if they want us to validate.
support-bot: Incident INC-4862 created by Alex R (priority: P1, component: eng-runtime).
Jessica L: thanks — please drop follow-up when staged. also capture exact client library versions and OS for the customer's environment.
Mira K: copied that. customer uses requests 2.31.0 on Ubuntu 20.04.
Alex R: test plan: add unit tests for parser with chunk sizes from 1..1024, add CI fuzzing with compressed input, and add telemetry to log per_query_counts validation mismatches.
SRE Jon: once patched, we'll run a backfill on logs to find any other requests that may have been silently misparsed.
Mira K: marking this thread for escalation. assigning to eng-runtime, SRE Jon and Alex R on the fix path.
eng-runtime: acknowledged. we'll keep thread updated with canary link and rollback plan. :shipit:
Mira K: thanks everyone — customer notified and workaround applied on their side.
Alex R: will post CI green and canary URL here when available.
eng-runtime: canary deployed to staging at 2054503500. preliminary checks show no mismatch for compressed tests. rolling to prod after 1h of monitoring.
Mira K: last update — prod roll started. will update when complete. :white_check_mark:
